correctness.rationale: Quadratic Schwarz lemma bounds |ω|≤k|z|²; odd analytic distortion integrates to T. Equality for a positive radius forces extremal third coefficient a3=1 in odd schlicht φ, hence φ=z/(1−z²) and ω=+kz² with h−g=φ. The equality F=H+bar G is locally orientation preserving but its slit-domain boundary real parts have opposing signs and horizontal coordinate derivative (1−k²|z|⁴)/|1−kz²|²>0, yielding two distinct preimages of iy for y>1/2. Closed normalized schlicht analytic combinations, derivative bounds and preservation of positive local degrees under uniform limit make the global univalent class compact; excluded equality therefore yields strict positive gap. k=0 analytic ψ attains.
residual_risks: No explicit M(k,r), only its strict inequality and existence; finite collision sample is not proof.

Classical harmonic shears and odd schlicht distortion
value.rationale: Corrects a mathematically substantive sharpness assertion in a current theorem: a locally sense-preserving equality shear cannot be used as a globally injective extremizer. The geometric double-preimage obstruction and compactness give genuinely better guaranteed distortion constants for every fixed positive parameter, even without closed optimum formula.
residual_risks: Quantitative gap size and endpoint asymptotics remain unknown.

final_claim: For normalized globally univalent odd sense-preserving harmonic maps with |ω|≤k<1 and one analytic univalent combination, sharp published radial envelope T(k,r) is attained only at k=0; for every 0<k,r<1 an attained optimal M(k,r) satisfies M(k,r)<T(k,r), while dropping global injectivity permits the positive-k equality shear.
limitations: Strict gap is qualitative for fixed k,r, not a uniform explicit constant or a theorem about larger harmonic classes.
